name: registry.delete
description: Delete a registry value or whole key. With `value` supplied, deletes just that value; without, deletes the entire key (and its subkeys recursively if `recursive: true`).

value.description: Optional value name. When supplied, deletes just that value (the parent key is preserved). When omitted, deletes the whole key.

recursive.description: When deleting a whole key (no `value`): if true, deletes subkeys recursively (analogous to reg.exe DELETE /F /S). Without this, deleting a key with subkeys returns ERR not_empty.

x-implementations.name: reg_delete_key_ex
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegDeleteKeyExW` for the whole-key non-recursive case (NT 5.2+; the agent picks 32-vs-64-bit view explicitly via samDesired).

x-implementations.name: reg_delete_tree
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegDeleteTreeW` for the recursive case (Vista+). NT 5.0/5.1/5.2 don't have RegDeleteTree; agent emulates via recursive enumeration + RegDeleteKey.

windows-modern.description: RegDeleteValueW for the single-value case; RegDeleteTreeW (Vista+) for recursive whole-key delete. Pre-Vista (NT 5.0/5.1/5.2 in modern's lineage) emulates recursive delete via RegEnumKeyExW walk + RegDeleteKeyExW.

windows-classic.description: RegDeleteValueW + RegDeleteKeyW (no Ex variant pre-NT-5.2). Recursive delete always emulated via enumeration. Win 9x lacks SeRestorePrivilege gating; classic agent's permission errors map to ERR permission_denied uniformly.
